Let me analyze the teaching examples more carefully to derive the correction rules.

Looking at Example 1 (2025-01-06):
- History: prices went from 68.31 (low) up to 75.94 (high)
- Model forecast: starts at 73.77, then declines to ~68.91
- True outcomes: start at 74.36, climb to ~79.75

The model is consistently BELOW true outcomes by about 3-6 points initially, and the gap increases over time.

Example 2 (2025-01-03):
- History: starts at 75.19 (near the peak of example 1's rise)
- Model forecast: starts at 75.44, then declines
- True outcomes: 75.94+, continuing to climb

Example 3 (2024-05-06):
- History: prices around 62-75
- Model forecast: starts at 73.09, declines
- True outcomes: 73.67+, climbing to 76-77

Example 4 (2024-05-03):
- History: similar to example 3
- Model forecast: starts at 72.13, declines
- True outcomes: 71.84... then climbing to 76-77

Example 5 (2024-05-10):
- History: starts at 74.25
- Model forecast: starts at 71.02, declines
- True outcomes: 71.59+, climbing to 76-77
